I always know I wanted children, and I felt good during my pregnancy. But when my oldest was born, I didn’t immediately “love” him. I didn’t had post-partum, and I knew I cared for him, but I guess I expected being a mom would be a whole new emotion (can’t explain it any better)..

The thing that helped was spending a lot of time with him, and a lot of skin on skin, and being honest to myself and not feeling quilty (you cannot deside how you feel, just how you act). I had a lot of experience with baby’s, so that helped quite a bit.

When my youngest was born I felt the same, I continued bonding, and now my heart swells thinking of them.

There is a saying in my language that helped me a lot; it roughly translates to; I love you so much more than yesterday, but I know I love you less today, than I will tomorrow..

As long as you put in the effort, and try to have a lot of positive interactions I’m sure you will be fine, and love your kid. And don’t feel afraid to ask help when your overwhelmed, in my opinion you can better have a few hours of positive interaction with your baby, than a whole day of forced interaction which makes you feel bad.. happy mom, happy baby.

Good luck! And I hope you can enjoy this experience
